questions.question: The famous tribal revolt of _________ took place in 1906 in Assam against British policies.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Songram Sangma.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Songram Sangma**

 
 
• **​**One of the most important rebellions against the British in **Assam in 1906 **was led by Songram Sangma.
 
• The** British's exploitation** of the tribes deprives them of their **traditional forest rights,** which led to this revolt.
 
• The British **forcibly relocated** the tribal people who were dispersed within the **deep forests **to a small land where they could better control them.
 
• The tribal people relied on forests as a **source of income,** so the British laws governing forests had a significant impact on their lives.
 
• The British declared all forests to be **state property** and designated some as reserved, prohibiting tribal people from** hunting, cultivating,** or** fruit-collecting** in these areas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other tribal movements**

 
 
• **Saflas** raided British plains subjects in **1835**, and they **revolted** once more between **1872 and 1973.**
 
• The Mishimis **murdered** Griffith, a **botanist**, and two missionaries in **1836.**
 
• There was a **Khampti** uprising in Assam from **1839 to 1842**, during which they attacked and killed British Agent **Adam White** and 80 other officers and soldiers.
 
• The **Syntengs** of the **Jaintia Hills** revolted from **1860 to 1862.**

questions.question: Which of the following laws works in constant pressure?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Charle’s law.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Charle’s law**

 
 
• ​**Charles's law **states that the **volume of an ideal gas is directly proportional to the absolute temperature at constant pressure**. 
 
• When the** pressure** that is applied to a sample of a **dry gas** is maintained at the same level, the law also states that the **Kelvin temperature** and the volume will be directly proportional.
 
• **Jacques Charles**, a French physicist, drafted this law in **1780**. His unpublished work provided a comprehensive description of this law.
 
• The **ideal gas** law is a special case of Charle's law.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Boyle’s law**

 
 
• ​Boyle's law is a gas law that says that a gas's pressure is** inversely proportional **to its volume when it has a given mass and is kept at a constant temperature.
 
 
 
• **Thomson’s law**
 
 
• ​Along the length of a material rod whose ends are at different temperatures, **heat power (Qτ) is absorbed or evolved.**
 
• The temperature gradient along the **rod** and the **current flow** were found to be inversely correlated with this heat.
 
 
 
• **Graham’s law**
 
 
• ​A gas's rate of** diffusion or effusion** is** inversely proportional** to the square root of its **molecular weight,** according to Graham's law.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an oscillatory motion?

options.text: Moving of an object in a straight line
Moving of a bus in a circular path
To and fro motion of a simple pendulum
Dropping of an object from a height

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To and fro motion of a simple pendulum.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Oscillatory motion**

__
 
• **​**The** to-and-fro **movement of an object from its mean position is referred to as oscillatory motion.
 
• In a perfect world, the object would be able to oscillate indefinitely without encountering any** friction**; however, in the real world, this is not possible, and the object must come to an** equilibrium.**
 
• **Examples** of oscillatory motion are as follows:
 
 
• Oscillation of **simple pendulum**
 
• **Vibrating strings** of musical instruments are a mechanical example of oscillatory motion
 
• Movement of **spring**
 
• **Alternating current** is an electrical example of oscillatory motion
 
• A series of oscillations are seen in** the cosmological model**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Simple Harmonic Motion**

 
• A type of oscillatory motion known as simple harmonic motion (SHM) is defined as a particle moving along a** straight line** at an acceleration that is** inversely proportional **to the distance from a fixed point on the line.
 
• A **restoring force** that complies with **Hooke's law** is required to bring any simple mechanical harmonic system (such as the weight hanging from the spring to the wall) back to its **equilibrium position.**
 
• There are two types of **Simple Harmonic Motion (SHM):**
 
 
• **Linear SHM**: Simple harmonic motion is referred to as linear when a particle moves in a **straight line** around a fixed point (called equilibrium position).
 
• **Angular SHM**: An angular simple harmonic motion occurs when a system moves **long and angularly** with respect to a fixed axis.

questions.question: Probiotics can be defined as:

options.text: endotoxin producing bacteria, which can lead to diarrhoea
live microorganisms that are intended to have health benefits when consumed or applied to the body
live microorganisms that pose a health threat when consumed or applied to the body

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__****Probiotics:**

__
 
• **Probiotics **are **live microorganisms **that are intended to **enhance health**.
 
• They can be found in **yoghurt **and other **fermented foods**, **dietary supplements**, and **cosmetics**. ***Hence Option 3 is correct.***
 
• Although bacteria and other microorganisms are sometimes thought of as **harmful **"**germs**," many of them are in fact **helpful**.
 
• Some bacteria help with **food digestion**, the production of **vitamins**, and the **destruction of disease-causing cells.**
 
• Numerous **probiotic bacteria **are identical to or nearly related to those that **naturally occur in our bodies.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• In probiotics, **various bacteria **could be present.
 
• The most common types of bacteria are those from the families **Lactobacillus **and **Bifidobacterium**.
 
• Other bacteria as well as yeasts like **Saccharomyces boulardii **may be used as probiotics.
 
• There are many different types of probiotics, and each has **potential effects**.
 
• For instance, just because one **strain **of **Lactobacillus **helps prevent a disease** doesn't mean that all strains of the bacteria** or all probiotics from the **Bifidobacterium **genus will do the same.

questions.question: What is the mass number of nitrogen?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__14.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

**Nitrogen: **

__
 
• **Nitrogen** is a chemical element with the** symbol N, atomic number 7 and mass number 14.**
 
• Nitrogen is a **non-metal **and the **lightest element **in **group 15 **of the periodic table, also referred to as **pnictogens**.
 
• It is a **common element **in the universe and is thought to rank ninth in terms of overall abundance in both the Milky Way and the Solar System.
 
• At standard pressure and temperature, two of the element's atoms combine to form N₂, a **colourless **and **odourless diatomic gas**.
 
• N₂ is the most common **uncombined element **and makes up most of the Earth's atmosphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

**Mass Number: **

 
• The total number of **protons **and **neutrons **in an atom's nucleus is known as the **mass number.**
 
• For instance, **uranium-235 **and **uranium-238** are the names of the two most well-known isotopes of uranium, those having mass numbers 235 and 238, respectively.
 
• Each **isotope **of an element is represented by the same literal symbol and has the same atomic number (number of protons).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

**Operation Flood:**

__
 
• **Operation Flood **was** **initiated in** 1970 **and** **has aided **dairy farmers **in taking charge of their own development and claiming ownership of the resources they produce.
 
• The aims of Operation Flood were as follows:
 
 
• A surge in milk production ("flood of milk");
 
• To boost rural incomes and;
 
• Provide consumers with cheap prices.

questions.question: In India, what type of unemployment is created due to lack of employable skills among the educated youths in India?

__
 
• **Structural Unemployment:** In India, structural unemployment occurs when there is a mismatch between the skills that workers possess and the skills required for available jobs. This often affects educated youth who may have qualifications but lack the employable skills demanded by the market.
 
• **Education vs. Employability:** Despite a growing number of educated individuals, many lack the specific skills required for modern industries, leading to a form of structural unemployment.

__
 
• **Long-term Unemployment:** Structural unemployment tends to persist over time if workers do not adapt to changing job requirements, leading to long-term unemployment.
 
• **Need for Skill Development:** To reduce structural unemployment, it is essential to provide skill development programs that align with industry demands and technological advancements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Global Phenomenon:** Structural unemployment is not unique to India; many countries experience this issue due to rapid technological changes and evolving economic structures.
 
• **Solution:** Governments and institutions often focus on reskilling and upskilling programs to help bridge the gap between available jobs and the current workforce.
